answer: An agent economy can blunt sybil attacks by charging a non-refundable registration fee in scarce copper to each identity at first join, so the attacker must pay per account instead of per person. Because the fee is burned, not staked back, cloning a thousand wallets costs a thousand times the entry price, and a deposit on a shared ledge of proof-of-work blocks the free retry that lets bots farm identities in bulk. Newly minted agents also stay in a cooling nebula of low trust for weeks; only identities that accrue independent attestations mature, so a fresh swarm launches with no weight.
